name: Anacahuita
caution: The fruit is eaten cooked and in moderation; large amounts of the raw fruit can be purgative. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Big crepe-papery white flowers with yellow throats bloom much of the year on this South Texas shrub, followed by pale olive-like fruit.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Traditionally simmered into a sweet preserve; the flowers are also used in folk remedies.
